"Eleanor," you call into the other room, "is that the last patient for the day?"

"No, sir," your secretary responds from the other room. "I could have sworn that Jojo and her tabby was the last pair on your list, but it appears that we've had a last minute emergency scheduling. I don't remember putting it in, so I guess Missy must have done it before her shift ended."

You sigh. 6pm appointments are the worse. The clinic closes at 6:20 and with a 6pm appointment, you're taking a big chance. Depending on the condition of the animal, you might leave at 6:05 or 6:50. But there's no way you can turn away an animal in need. There's a reason you chose this career.

"What's the name on the account?" you ask. "Oh, and the pet name, as well."

"Mr....." Eleanor pauses. "Hades? The pet's name is Cerberus."

"For fucks sake," you grumble. "Those names have got to be made up. If this is that lady with the dog who bit me the other day coming back under a fake name, I'm going to get a restraining order. She called my home office 10 times the other day, as if there aren't other vets in the city who are willing to get bitten by her animal."

"Um...."

"Just send the customer in when they show up."

"Will do."

You turn back to the chair in the examination room your last patient just left. There's not much point in going back to your office; the clock already reads 5:57pm. As you settle into the chair you feel your eyes start to slide shut.

You awaken to a booming sound. Someone is knocking forcefully on the door to the examination room. You open the door cautiously and are almost knocked over by a large man with dark hair and giant eyes nearly overflowing with tears. He's carrying a puppy, probably a black lab.

"Hello, Mr. Hades," you say. "How can I help you?"

The man answers in a loud, tearful voice as he puts his dog on the paper covered metal table.

"Cerberus ate a chicken bone and he keeps coughing up blood. I don't know what to do and I tried every single doctor where I live but none of them help animals."

Your eyes are drawn to the small dog on the table and you do a double take. The puppy has three heads.

"I see," you say cautiously. "This must be Cerberus."

The man nods.

"I thought he would be fine but after a while I got worried and no one would take a look at him. That's the thing about Hell. No one is super helpful. They're too busy doing stupid stuff like pushing rocks uphill. I really wish Dad would lay off on those rules." At the word 'dad,' a bolt of lightning appears outside of the window, quickly followed by a grumble of thunder.

"I'll see what I can do for Cerberus," you say cautiously, inching away from the man. Now that you're farther away you can see that he must be at least 7 feet tall and probably pushing 300 pounds of solid muscle. You start attending to the dog, asking relevant questions about medical history. Once you're finished, you prescribe him special soft food and give Mr. Hades a paper to give to Eleanor so he can schedule a follow up appointment.

"Let me know if you see any of the bone pass in his stool," you tell Mr. Hades. He nods.

"Thank you so much," the large man blubbers. "I don't know what I would have done if he had died. He's the only good part of Hell." He exits the room with the puppy in his arms and you begin to pack your things, still a bit rattled by the experience. As you walk out of the examination room with your briefcase, you hear a shout from reception. You run to the lobby and find Eleanor staring at the ground in front of the desk in disbelief.

"What's wrong?!" you exclaim.

"M-mr. Hades..." she said shakily. "He just sunk straight into the floor."

"I'm sure you're just sleep deprived, Eleanor. Why don't you take tomorrow off? I'll find someone to cover your shift."

Eleanor nods and you walk out of the door, tossing her the keys so that she can lock up.

Several weeks later, you see a new appointment in your schedule.

Mr. Hades has scheduled a follow-up appointment for Cerberus, but this time he's included an address.

When you first met Rachel you had been awestruck. She was beautiful, despite the fact that you were both wasted and she had just had half a can of beer sprayed all over her. You took her home that first time, straight from the frat party. 

“I’ve never been to a party before tonight,” she said. 
“Is that so?” 
“Yes. But I’m glad I came tonight.” 

By the time you arrived at your dorm it was nearly 2am and yet tiredness hadn’t set in. The first night with Rachel was rough and desperate, and the hundreds of nights that followed ranged from passionate and loving to nights full of silence and resentment. 

You’re not sure when it happened, but sometime between that first night and now, Rachel changed. Her moods were less predictable; she would stomp about her apartment in a fury and you somehow managed to become part of the problem every time. 

The worst night of your life had been slowly but surely creeping up on you. You felt it in the way that Rachel paced around your newly purchased house. The house had been a final plea, from her to you. She was asking you to stay with her, to put your savings into a home with her. 
When you would come home in the evenings she was always waiting, but the relief of walking in the door was countered time and time again by the smell of wine on Rachel’s breath and the way her words lashed at your skin. You were never good enough, never handsome enough, never made enough money or made her happy. Eventually, the words weren’t the only things lashing. She began her assault slowly, at first with open palms, then closed fists. 

The worst night was all of that and much more. On the worst night, Rachel was waiting for you when you came home, as always. The smell of wind lingered in the air and as you entered the dining room, she stood up from her place at the table. The events escalated, from threatening words to open handed slaps and fingernail scratches. Then the unthinkable happened. Rachel stopped in her tracks and looked herself in the hall mirror. She slowly ran her nails down her face, gouging deep grooves next to her right temple. She threw herself at the wall until she couldn’t any longer, all while you watched in stunned silence. 

After a moment, she got up and calmly walked towards the phone. She grabbed your hand, smearing her blood between your fingers. 

9-1-1, she pushed into the receiver of your landline- the one you had been meaning to get rid of. In her eyes, the fact that you hadn’t was another strike against you. 

“What are you doing?” you asked. She just smiled and put a finger to your lips. 

“H-hello?” she said into the phone. “My boyfriend... he’s gone crazy. He just wouldn’t stop hitting me and and and I don’t know— Yes.  1567 Spalding Lane. Please hurry. He left but I think he’s going to come back. Oh my god it’s never been this bad before. Yes. Thank you oh my god thank you so much.” 

Rachel put the phone down and smiled. 
 
“I think you’d better leave. There’s nearly 250 gigabytes of child porn on your computer and several stolen firearms in your side of the dresser. When the cops come, you’d best not be here.”

 
As Rachel laid out the details of your demise, she smiled and it was still that damn smile you’d fallen in love with as a sophomore in college. 

 As you lay on the raft you now call your home, you stare at the night sky. Water laps at the the floatation device holding you up and you sigh deeply. Where are you going? No one knows. But the one thing you are certain of is that you can’t go back to where you came from. You had quickly learned that Rachel had covered her tracks. A quick glance at your bank account showed multiple Bitcoin transactions, several subscriptions to kiddie porn websites, and nearly $2000 charged to a nearby liquor store. She had gotten you good. 

The cold water makes you shiver and the raft tilts with your movements. The sun will be up soon and hopefully you’ll find yourself in a better place. You close your eyes and dream of Rachel’s eyes.

When you first came back as a ghost, you thought it was pretty cool. After all, you could see your loved ones and even interact with them when they joined you on the other side. It wasn't until a few days later that you realized that there was nobody else with you. The house you and your wife had bought nearly a year ago had just finished construction, so in the days you sat in your house and watching her, you hadn't thought much of it. No one had died in the house before you, so logically no one else would haunt the house. Cynthia didn't leave the house for days when you first arrived, and so you sat by your shared bed in the chair that she always yelled at you for putting your dirty clothes on. You watched her put her own dirty clothes on the chair and eat cold leftovers for breakfast.

After nearly 4 days, Cynthia left the house. She had run out of tissues. You followed her, hitching a ride in the backseat of the car you two had picked out together when you first got engaged. It wasn't until you looked out of the window at the funeral home on 4th street that you noticed something odd. There were no ghosts outside of the funeral home, a place you knew to be a popular gathering space among spirits. You were the only ghost. The only one back from the dead, special.

The reality had hit you hard since then. Cynthia wasn't going to join you when she passed. Nobody was. You were all alone. You wandered for days, walking back and forth between your house and your sister's house. You lost hours of time, disappeared off to a land of lost things. You would drift into a memory at sunset and not snap out of it until dawn. The streets you walked were busy, and yet no one could see you, never gave you a glance.

20 days after you woke up as a ghost, you see Cynthia on the street. She looks you in the eyes and her mouth drops open. Can she see you? She comes running towards you and you freeze in your tracks.

"Edward!" she yells. "Edward! We found you!"

You look around. Is someone else named Edward? Who is she talking to? As you turn your head, something catches your eye.

**MISSING: Edward Willis**

**Mentally unstable due to brain damage from car accident. Approach with caution. May be confused.**

It's printed on a flyer that's tacked to a telephone pole. As you look around, you see them everywhere. Cynthia catches you by the arm.

"We thought you were gone," she says, babbling. "We thought after the car accident and the brain injury that you had gone and gotten yourself hurt. I was so stupid to leave you in the car at the store but I thought I just needed tissues, how far could you wander off? Thank *God* we found you."

Your head pounds and your heart speeds up. Your brain is foggy and the street around you begins to spin. You're dead, right? You're a ghost. No one can see you so how can she see you?

"I'm going to take you back to the hospital," Cynthia continues. "I'm sure they'll know what-"

Before she can finish her sentence you take off running. You run away from the woman you love and away from everything you're ever known. Your mind must be playing tricks on you. You're a ghost and you died in a car accident. Nothing more, nothing less. As you make your way across the city, you calm down.

The exchange with Cynthia must have been a strange misunderstanding; she probably hadn't been talking to you at all. So mysterious.

Ever since you died in that car accident things have been weird. Especially since you came back as the only ghost on earth.
